knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

The `dppca` package combines **private PC directions, private variance estimates along those directions, and private score histograms** to construct five PCA visualizations: **scree, loading, score, variable, and biplot**. This article describes how these visualizations are constructed from DP estimates, what information each plot represents, and how their interpretations differ from those of ordinary PCA. Particular attention is given to the DP variable plot and biplot, which combine multiple private quantities.

For background on ordinary PCA visualizations, see [PCA Background](method-pca-background.html). The underlying DP estimation methods are described in [DP Directions Methodology](method-dp-loading.html), [DP Scree Methodology](method-dp-scree.html), and [DP Score Methodology](method-dp-score.html). For implementation details, plotting options, and examples, see the [DP PCA Visualization Tutorial](tutorials-dp-visualization.html).

## 1. What is estimated privately? {#private-quantities}

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ contain observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^p$ in its rows. For clarity, suppose that
`dp_pca()` retains the first $k$ components and displays two selected axes `axes = c(a, b)`, with $a\ne b$ and $a,b\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$.

The integrated procedure uses the following quantities:

<style>
.dp-pca-table table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) { width: 25% !important; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) { width: 20% !important; }
.dp-pca-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) { width: 55% !important; }
</style>

::: {.dp-pca-table}

| Quantity | Notation | Role |
|:--|:--|:--|
| DP PC directions | $\widetilde{V}=(\widetilde{v}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{v}_p)$ | Define the common PC axes and loading coefficients. |
| DP eigenvalues | $\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k$ | Determine scree/PVE and scale variable and biplot coordinates. |
| DP score frame | $\widetilde{F}$ | Defines the two-dimensional plotting region. |
| DP score histogram | $\widetilde{h}$ | Describes the distribution of projected observations without releasing individual coordinates. |
| Synthetic score points | $s_1^*,\ldots,s_N^*$ | Provide a point-based view sampled from $\widetilde{h}$. |
:::

The mathematical definitions and estimation procedures for these quantities are described in the corresponding articles: [DP Directions Methodology](method-dp-loading.html) for DP PC directions, [DP Scree Methodology](method-dp-scree.html) for DP eigenvalues, and [DP Score Methodology](method-dp-score.html) for the DP score frame, histogram, and synthetic score sampling. These five quantities are used to construct five DP PCA visualizations: scree, loading, score, variable, and biplot.

## 2. Privacy budget and shared estimation {#privacy-accounting}

Write the total privacy budget as $(\varepsilon,\delta)$. The integrated
procedure requires allocations for `loading`, `scree`, and `score`:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_L+\varepsilon_S+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}&=\varepsilon,\\
\delta_L+\delta_S+\delta_{\mathrm{score}}&=\delta.
\end{aligned}
$$

Within the score allocation, the package uses

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_F&=0.35\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}},
&\delta_F&=0,\\
\varepsilon_H&=0.65\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}},
&\delta_H&=\delta_{\mathrm{score}},
\end{aligned}
$$

where $F$ denotes the private **frame** and $H$ the private **histogram**. 
The frame budget is shared equally among two private coordinate medians and a private radial quantile.

The resulting estimation flow is
$$
\begin{gathered}
X\ \longrightarrow\ \widetilde{V}\quad\text{(loading budget)},\\
(X,\widetilde{V})\ \longrightarrow\ 
\widetilde{\lambda}_{1:k}\quad\text{(scree budget)},\\
(X,\widetilde{V})\ \longrightarrow\
\widetilde{F}\ \longrightarrow\ \widetilde{h}
\quad\text{(score budget)},\\
(\widetilde{V},\widetilde{\lambda}_{1:k},\widetilde{F},\widetilde{h})
\ \longrightarrow\ \text{five PCA displays}.
\end{gathered}
$$

Only **one** direction matrix, **one** selected scree method, and **one** selected histogram method are estimated within an integrated fit. 


## 3. Five DP PCA Visualization


The five DP PCA visualizations are scree, loading, score, variable, and biplot. The construction of the DP scree, loading, and score plots is described in [DP Directions Methodology](method-dp-loading.html), [DP Scree Methodology](method-dp-scree.html), and [DP Score Methodology](method-dp-score.html), respectively. Therefore, this section focuses on the construction and interpretation of the DP variable plot and DP biplot.


### 3.1. DP variable plot (correlation-style coordinates) {#dp-variable-visualization}

In ordinary PCA, a variable plot represents the correlations between the original variables and the PC scores. As described in [Section 4.4 of PCA Background](method-pca-background.html#variable-plot), the correlation between variable $j$ and the $\ell$th PC score is

$$
\operatorname{Cor}(X_{\cdot j},S_{\cdot\ell})
=
\frac{\sqrt{\widehat\lambda_\ell}\,\widehat v_{j\ell}}
{\widehat\sigma_j},
$$

where $\widehat\lambda_\ell$ and $\widehat v_{j\ell}$ are the sample eigenvalue and loading coefficient, respectively, and $\widehat\sigma_j$ is the sample standard deviation of variable $j$.

In the DP setting, these empirical quantities cannot be directly released without accounting for their privacy costs. Instead, `dp_pca()` constructs the variable plot using privately estimated PC directions and eigenvalues.

Let $\widetilde{V}_k=(\widetilde{v}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{v}_k)$ denote the first $k$ private PC directions, and let $\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k$ be the corresponding nonnegative private eigenvalues. These quantities define a DP-based covariance approximation,

$$
\widetilde{\Sigma}_k
=
\widetilde{V}_k
\operatorname{diag}
(\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k)
\widetilde{V}_k^\top.
$$

Therefore, the implied variance of variable $j$ is 

$$
\widetilde{\sigma}_{j,k}^2
=
(\widetilde{\Sigma}_k)_{jj}
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{k}
\widetilde{\lambda}_\ell\widetilde{v}_{j\ell}^{\,2}.
$$

Using this quantity in place of the sample variance, we define the DP correlation coordinate of variable $j$ along PC $\ell$ as

$$
\widetilde{r}_{j\ell}
=
\frac{
\sqrt{\widetilde{\lambda}_\ell}\,\widetilde{v}_{j\ell}
}{
\widetilde{\sigma}_{j,k}
},
\qquad
\widetilde{\sigma}_{j,k}>0.
$$

For two selected components $a$ and $b$, the DP variable plot represents variable $j$ by

$$
R_j^{\mathrm{DP}}
=
(\widetilde{r}_{ja},\widetilde{r}_{jb}).
$$

Variables with zero implied variance are omitted because their coordinates are undefined.

As in the ordinary variable plot, the DP coordinates lie inside or on the unit circle. Indeed,

$$
\|R_j^{\mathrm{DP}}\|_2^2
=
\widetilde{r}_{ja}^{\,2}
+
\widetilde{r}_{jb}^{\,2}
=
\frac{
\widetilde{\lambda}_a\widetilde{v}_{ja}^{\,2}
+
\widetilde{\lambda}_b\widetilde{v}_{jb}^{\,2}
}{
\displaystyle\sum_{\ell=1}^{k}
\widetilde{\lambda}_\ell\widetilde{v}_{j\ell}^{\,2}
}
\le 1.
$$

The squared distance from the origin measures how much of the reconstructed variance of variable $j$ is attributed to the two displayed PCs, relative to all $k$ retained PCs. Variables near the unit circle have most of their reconstructed variance associated with the displayed PCs, whereas variables near the origin have more of their reconstructed variance associated with the other retained PCs.

The angles between variable vectors can provide information about their associations in the displayed PC plane. Vectors pointing in similar directions suggest positive associations, while vectors pointing in opposite directions suggest negative associations. Approximately perpendicular vectors indicate weak associations within the displayed plane. These interpretations are most informative when the variables are well represented by the selected components.


### 3.2. DP biplot {#dp-biplot-visualization}

A **biplot** displays observations and variables simultaneously in a low-dimensional representation of the data. In ordinary PCA, as described in [Section 4.5 of PCA Background](method-pca-background.html#biplot), the biplot coordinates are constructed from the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the centered data matrix. For two selected components $a$ and $b$, the observation and variable coordinates are given by

$$
G_\alpha=U_ID_I^{1-\alpha},
\qquad
H_\alpha=V_ID_I^\alpha,
\qquad 0\le\alpha\le1,
$$

where $I=\{a,b\}$ and $D_I=\operatorname{diag}(d_a,d_b)$ contains the corresponding singular values. The parameter $\alpha$ determines how the singular-value scaling is distributed between observations and variables.

In the DP setting, `dp_pca()` constructs a **DP biplot** using synthetic score points generated from the private score histogram, together with privately estimated PC directions and eigenvalues. 
Recall that the singular values in ordinary PCA satisfy $d_\ell=\sqrt{(n-1)\widehat\lambda_\ell}$.
Accordingly, we define the corresponding DP-based scaling factors as

$$
\widetilde{d}_\ell
=
\sqrt{(n-1)\widetilde{\lambda}_\ell},
\qquad \ell\in\{a,b\},
$$

where $\widetilde{\lambda}_\ell\ge0$ denotes the private eigenvalues and $n$ is the original sample size.

Let $s_i^*=(s_{ia}^*,s_{ib}^*)$ denote the $i$th synthetic score point generated from the private histogram, and let $\widetilde{v}_{j\ell}$ denote the coefficient of variable $j$ in the $\ell$th private PC direction. For $\widetilde{d}_\ell>0$, the DP biplot coordinates are defined by

$$
G_{i\ell}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
=
\frac{s_{i\ell}^*-c_\ell^{\mathrm{disp}}}
{\widetilde{d}_\ell^\alpha},
\qquad
H_{j\ell}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
=
\widetilde{v}_{j\ell}\widetilde{d}_\ell^\alpha,
$$

where $c_\ell^{\mathrm{disp}}$ is the display-centering adjustment defined in [Section 8.1 of DP Score Methodology](method-dp-score.html#score-display-centering), with its two coordinates corresponding to the selected PC axes $a$ and $b$, respectively.

With `center = TRUE` (the default), the synthetic scores are translated relative to the private frame center, and the variable arrows originate at $(0,0)$. With `center = FALSE`, the scores remain unshifted, and the variable arrows originate at the private frame center expressed in the alpha-transformed coordinates.


For the two selected components, the rows $G_i^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
=
\left(
G_{ia}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha),
G_{ib}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
\right)$
represent synthetic observations, while $H_j^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
=
\left(
H_{ja}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha),
H_{jb}^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
\right)$
represent the original variables through their private direction coefficients.

As in ordinary PCA, the parameter $\alpha$ controls the relative scaling of the observation and variable coordinates:

- **$\alpha=0$:** Observation coordinates retain the synthetic score scale (apart from optional centering), and variable coordinates are the private PC direction coefficients.
- **$\alpha=1/2$:** The DP-based singular-value scaling is shared symmetrically between observations and variables.
- **$\alpha=1$:** Variable coordinates are multiplied by the full DP-based singular-value factors, while synthetic score coordinates are divided by them.


**Arrow scaling.** To display observations and variable vectors on a common plotting region, `dp_pca()` applies an additional scaling factor to the variable vectors.

Let
$$
r_G
=
Q_{0.9}
\left(
\left\{
\left\|
G_i^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
-
\overline G^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
\right\|_2
\right\}_{i=1}^{N}
\right)
$$

denote the empirical 90th percentile of the distances of the synthetic score points from their mean, and let

$$
r_H
=
\max_{1\le j\le p}
\left\|
H_j^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha)
\right\|_2.
$$

The common arrow scaling factor is

$$
\gamma
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{r_G}{r_H}, & r_G>0,\ r_H>0,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

Therefore, the displayed variable vectors are $\widetilde{H}_j^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha) = \gamma H_j^{\mathrm{DP}}(\alpha).$

**Ordinary reference.**
For comparison, `non_private = TRUE` asks the package to compute ordinary
PCA from the sample covariance matrix. Let $\widehat V$ and
$\widehat\lambda_\ell$ be its directions and eigenvalues. Its scores are
sample-mean centered, $S=(X-\mathbf1_n\bar x^\top)\widehat V.$




## 4. Summary

<style>
.dppca-plot-table table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.dppca-plot-table colgroup col:nth-child(1) { width: 15% !important; }
.dppca-plot-table colgroup col:nth-child(2) { width: 25% !important; }
.dppca-plot-table colgroup col:nth-child(3) { width: 60% !important; }
</style>

::: {.dppca-plot-table}


| Plot | DP quantities used | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Scree / PVE** | $\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k$ | Shows the relative importance of the estimated PCs. PVE is normalized over the $k$ retained components. |
| **Loading** | $\widetilde{V}$ | Shows how the original variables contribute to the private PC directions. |
| **Score** | $\widetilde{F}$, $\widetilde{h}$, and $s_1^*,\ldots,s_N^*$ | Shows the distribution of projected observations without directly releasing their individual scores. |
| **Variable** | $\widetilde{V}_k$ and $\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k$ | Shows relationships among variables implied by the private covariance approximation, rather than their exact empirical correlations. |
| **Biplot** | $\widetilde{V}$, $\widetilde{\lambda}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\lambda}_k$, and $s_1^*,\ldots,s_N^*$  | Provides a joint view of the private score distribution and variable directions, with additional scaling for visualization. |
:::


The five DP PCA visualizations can be generated using `dp_pca()` and
`plot()`, which reuse the estimated private quantities across the plots.
For implementation details, plotting options, and examples, see the
[DP PCA Visualization Tutorial](tutorials-dp-visualization.html).
